consumer: The delivery quest's mission completion check (engine mission::is_complete / item-requirement predicate) asking 'does the player satisfy the quest's required item?' to drive the HUD's satisfied/not-satisfied indicator.
scope: The mission requirement's own reachable scope (the engine's required-item predicate over the inventory it counts), not merely items physically on the avatar.
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_carried_items — it dumps raw wielded/worn/inventory items on the avatar (a simulation-state listing), re-deriving satisfaction from a partial carried-only view instead of returning the mission predicate's computed result.
divergence: The required item sits in adjacent reachable inventory (e.g. vehicle cargo or an open container the mission predicate counts): the engine's quest check reports satisfied, but carried_items[] (avatar-only) omits it, so the HUD wrongly shows the requirement unmet.
